exposure: Auditory brainstem response (ABR) threshold (normal, mild, moderate, severe subgroups)
Quantitative T1 values in inferior colliculus (IC)
Quantitative T1 values in lateral lemniscus (LL)
Quantitative T1 values in middle cerebellar peduncle (MCP)
outcome: Brain changes (alterations in gray and white matter)
Elevated quantitative T1 values in specific brain regions (IC, LL, MCP)
cohort: The study participants included children diagnosed with SNHL and a control group of children with normal hearing.
finding: Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and inner ear malformation were associated with SNHL onset, and children with moderate/severe SNHL and those with IEM exhibited elevated T1 values and reduced white matter metrics in specific brain regions, with LL-T1 and WMF identified as independent risk factors for SNHL.
